disclaimer: Numerical Monte Carlo evidence for one lattice ensemble (finite lattice spacing, finite volume, statistical errors only). Not a proof of the Yang-Mills mass gap.
rules: pre-registered rules R1-R8, see the docstring of ym/stats.py

stream_consistency.note: plaquette means of the individual streams, each with the error from its own integrated autocorrelation time; chi2 about their weighted mean

caveats: Plateau rule R5 chooses t* with the same data that give m_eff(t*): the quoted jackknife error does not include this selection effect. Synthetic tests at production-like signal-to-noise found 52-65 % of the results within 1 sigma of the truth (nominal 68 %), 91-97 % within 2 sigma, rms pull 1.1-1.2. Always read the fixed-t values (blocks 'fixed_t', 'meff_table') next to the R5 value, treat m_eff(1) - m_eff(2) as a systematic uncertainty, and do not claim agreement or disagreement with other results at the 1 sigma level from the R5 number alone.
m_eff(t*) of a positive correlator is a variational UPPER estimate of the ground-state energy; its error is statistical only.
A value flagged 'upper_bound_only' ('no plateau') is not a measurement and must not be quoted as one; rule R5 has no significance requirement on the correlator itself.
One lattice spacing and one volume: no continuum or infinite-volume extrapolation is contained in this file. Numerical evidence, not a proof of the mass gap.

ratios.note: jackknife error with the glueball mass and the torelon energy taken from the same bins (correlations included); both t* held fixed

D4.note: a*Lambda_L from the two-loop asymptotic-scaling formula (ym/exact.py); asymptotic scaling is known to be violated at accessible beta
